headline: State Park Lodging and River Permits
reservation: Campsites and the Mohican State Park Lodge require separate reservations through the Ohio DNR portal. Private glamping sites in Loudonville operate under independent booking systems. While park entry is generally free, specific river activities or high-demand lodging windows should be secured months in advance.

days.title: Gorge Depths and Waterfalls

stops.name: Lyons Falls Trail
stops.detail: Hike through the hemlocks to reach Big and Little Lyons Falls within the Clear Fork Gorge.

stops.name: Pleasant Hill Dam
stops.detail: View the 'morning glory' spillway and the transition from the lake to the river.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local park roads; walking is the primary mode between sites.
days.note: Waterfall flow is highly dependent on recent rainfall; may be a trickle in late summer.

days.title: River Views and Historic Heights

stops.name: Mohican State Park Fire Tower
stops.detail: Climb for a panoramic view of the hardwood canopy and the winding Mohican River.

stops.name: Clear Fork Gorge Overlook
stops.detail: Observe the 300-foot deep gorge from a stable, wheelchair-accessible viewpoint.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to navigate between the southern and northern park entrances.
days.note: Fire tower access is seasonal and may close during high winds or maintenance.

days.title: River Drift and Valley Exploration

stops.name: Mohican River
stops.detail: Launch a canoe or tube for a slow-paced float through the Mohican-Memorial State Forest.

stops.name: Covered Bridge
stops.detail: Visit the restored Smith's Mill bridge for a classic North Central Ohio architectural landmark.

days.driving: Allow for local transfer to canoe liveries; river travel time depends on water levels.
days.note: Check river gauges via official sources; high water can result in mandatory craft restrictions.

intel.title: Trail Safety
intel.text: The Hemlock Path can be slippery and narrow near the gorge edge. Sturdy footwear is recommended for all gorge-level hiking.

intel.title: Fall Foliage Peak
intel.text: Peak colors typically occur in late October, drawing significant crowds. Visit on weekdays to avoid heavy congestion at the gorge overlooks.

intel.title: River Access Points
intel.text: Parking near the covered bridge and main river access points fills early on summer Saturdays. Use designated overflow lots near the state forest boundary if needed.

intel.title: Loudonville Services
intel.text: Full services including fuel and groceries are located in Loudonville. Do not expect supplies once deep within the State Forest sections.

intel.title: Variable Coverage
intel.text: Signal is generally stable at the Lodge but drops significantly in the bottom of the Clear Fork Gorge. Notify contacts of your itinerary before hiking.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Akron-Canton (CAK); proceed to Loudonville for local supplies before reaching the park lodge or campground.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are sufficient for all paved park roads and main overlooks.
plan.goldenHour: Clear Fork Gorge Overlook; best color occurs during the mid-autumn foliage season.
